record.one_liner: Help Scout is a customer support helpdesk (shared inbox, conversations, Docs knowledge base) with a public REST API.
record.auth_notes: Inbox API uses OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code and Client Credentials flows). Docs API uses an API key passed via HTTP Basic auth in the username field.
record.access_notes: critic: confirmed self_serve_trial. Help Scout docs state the Free plan does not include API access; API is on paid Standard/Plus/Pro, and the pricing page offers a 15-day no-card trial of Standard or Plus. OAuth apps are created self-serve under Your Profile > My apps; no review step documented.
record.api_notes: Base URL https://api.helpscout.net/v2. Inbox API 2.0 plus Docs API; Standard plan lacks reporting endpoints.
record.blocker_notes: critic: main_blocker paid_plan -> none, since a self-serve trial gives working credentials (verdict ready). Production use after the 15-day trial needs a paid plan. Official MCP is read-only for new connections, so writes need the Inbox API.

evidence.quote: This is an HTTPS-only API and it uses OAuth 2.0 authorization, implementing Authorization Code and Client Credential flows.
Authentication is based on API keys.
The Free plan does not include access to the API or integrations.
When you sign up for a free trial of the Standard or Plus plan, you’ll get 15 days to take all of the plan’s features for a test drive — no credit card required.
Help Scout MCP gives AI assistants secure, official access to Help Scout data.
Set the remote MCP server URL to https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp
The Client Credentials flow is meant for internal integrations.
Your Help Scout account must have API access, which is included on the Standard, Plus, and Pro plans.
